source.title: Transferred Discrepancy: Quantifying the Difference Between Representations
source.authors: Yunzhen Feng; Runtian Zhai; Di He; Li-Wei Wang; Bin Dong

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests representational similarity with a new, downstream-task-based measure (transferred discrepancy) and compares it with CCA and CKA; the reported results bear on seed convergence, metric/task dependence, and similarity across model scales.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own measured prediction disagreement or representation-dissimilarity results. The paper's cited findings are not recorded. It reports other metrics and training conditions, but omits some where they add no distinct result relevant to these versions or where table layout does not support reliable assignment.
record.test_reason: The study measures representation differences across independently initialized networks using downstream prediction disagreement, CCA, CKA, and cross-covariance singular values. Its own results test seed convergence, scale trends, metric and task dependence, and incomplete convergence. TD supplies a functional measure of representation similarity rather than identifying shared features directly.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors argue that representation similarity should be evaluated relative to downstream tasks, and find that independently initialized networks can make substantially different downstream predictions despite high CKA similarity. They associate greater prediction consistency with several training strategies and with larger ResNets. Their results do not establish that seed pairs share no features, nor a universal causal relationship between agreement and representation quality; adversarial training improves agreement despite lowering classification accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes and evaluates transferred discrepancy, a downstream-prediction-based measure, alongside CCA and CKA; it does not reproduce either original source's method.
record.method_sensitivity: TD varies with downstream task and training/upstream task; the reported metric values also differ between TD, CCA, and CKA. TDhard changes with augmentation, learning-rate schedule, adversarial training, architecture depth, and width.
record.problems: The main experiments use a narrow image-classification setting and mostly same-architecture seed pairs. Several reported averages have no uncertainty estimates. Prediction disagreement is an indirect measure of feature similarity, and the study does not establish whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted TDsoft values where the authors report trends similar to TDhard; omitted batch-size results in Table 12 and some extra metric values in Tables 9-14 because they were not needed for the version verdicts. Omitted the six sanity-check pair comparisons in Table 1 and the detailed eight-configuration augmentation results in Table 9; Table 3 provides the clearly described augmentation configurations used here.

untested.parts: Scale-dependent convergence between models differing in architecture families, training data, or objectives is not tested. Each comparison pairs seeds of one architecture; capability increases are quantified only for the ResNet depth endpoints.
No paired vision-language representations or cross-modal capability sweep.
No identification of shared individual features or comparison of neuron bases. Classification TD measures functional agreement indirectly; CCA and singular values supply subspace evidence.
No empirical representation mapping, stitching, relative representation, or unpaired interchangeability experiment.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
Neighbour-count and comparable metric-parameter sweeps are not tested. CIFAR-100 and SVHN evaluation inputs do test distribution changes, although task and input changes are not fully separated.
No demonstrated scaling plateau and no causal isolation of shared training data or objectives as the explanation for convergence.

missing.what: Evaluation-input dependence of CCA and CKA for fixed seed pairs: Cifar-5-trained pairs have DCCA/DCKA 0.6961/0.0835 on CIFAR-10 inputs, 0.8003/0.4210 on CIFAR-100, and 0.8663/0.6940 on SVHN. Cifar-2-trained pairs similarly change from 0.6931/0.0402 to 0.7533/0.3036 and 0.8330/0.6305. These directly demonstrate weaker measured alignment on different input distributions, beyond task-dependent TD.

Training-time similarity is nonmonotonic: the authors report that all four discrepancy curves drop after learning-rate decay and then rise again. No row captures this trajectory, and rows_left_out does not declare it.
missing.locator: Supplement D.3, Number of Training Epochs; Figure 3

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source of any supplied version. Row states primarily describe seed agreement when a row also tests V6 or V7; partial convergence supports those challenge versions rather than limiting them. Absolute values from differently defined metrics are not calibrated equivalents, but their different summaries and task sensitivity bear on V6. Explicitly declared omissions from Tables 9-14 are not re-listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Tests depth and width sweeps and VGG depth, but not independently trained models differing in objectives, training data, or modalities; capability is not systematically measured alongside every scale condition.
Tests different initializations of the same architecture and measures downstream prediction agreement, not shared feature identities or shared subspaces directly.
No representation mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired mapping test.
No test of recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Tests several similarity measures and downstream task choices, but not neighbourhood-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
Shows incomplete agreement for some seed pairs and task settings, but does not isolate shared training data or objectives as the cause of alignment.
